第 54 章 Managers and Culture经理与文化

Arjun Anand / 阿琼·阿南德

— 第 157 页 —

When I was pursuing my engineering degree, there were these hazing rituals in which those from a higher year bullied those of us who were just arriving. When I asked one of the seniors why they wanted to bully and haze us, he said that they do it because it was done to them. I never did get hazed, and so I never knew what that feeling was like, and so I never hazed anyone who was my junior either. What's funny to me is that we still do this now even when we're older and working in professional careers; we just call it the organization's culture.

当我读工程学位时，有那些欺凌仪式，高年级的人欺负我们这些刚到的。当我问一个高年级的人为什么要欺负我们，他说他们这么做是因为别人也对他们这么做过。我从没被欺凌过，所以我不知道那种感觉是什么，所以我也从没欺凌过比我低的人。对我来说好笑的是我们现在还在这么做，即使我们长大了、在职业生涯中工作；我们只是叫它组织文化。

In an organization, the people who your employees will turn to in order to see the "preferred interpretation" of the company's culture are the managers, leaders, and executives. These individuals are the day-to-day representation of any organization's culture, and thus, it is imperative for the success of an organization to set the tone for leadership. To this end, I wanted to share a few thoughts that I feel are important for a leader in an organization (as well as for the organization itself) to know in order to support and grow new leaders.

在一个组织中，你的员工会去找经理、领导和高管，看公司文化的「偏好解读」。这些人是任何组织文化的日常代表，因此为领导力定调对组织成功至关重要。为此，我想分享一些我觉得组织中领导（以及组织本身）需要知道的想法，以支持和培养新领导。

Manager Training经理培训

When moving someone along the management career path, it is important to understand where they've come from, what they want to achieve, and how it aligns with the organization's goals so that you can create plans for them. Training doesn't mean just providing good reading material; it means having learning events to teach managers good habits, cultivate the appropriate skills for their levels, and providing safe avenues of practice. This manager training is what will make the difference between your employees thriving or leaving in apathy.

当让一个人走上管理职业道路时，重要的是理解他们从哪里来、他们想实现什么、这怎么和组织目标对齐，这样你可以为他们创建计划。培训不只是提供好的阅读材料；它意味着有学习活动教经理好习惯、培养适合他们层级的技能、提供安全的练习途径。这种经理培训将决定你的员工是茁壮成长还是冷漠离职。

— 第 158 页 —

Failure as a Rite of Passage失败作为成人礼

Although as an individual contributor you are able to be more in control of the individual tasks that you have assigned to you, as a manager you are responsible for making your reports work efficiently, all the while keeping them happy. In doing this you will fail many times. How your organization responds to your shortcomings will dictate how you react to your direct reports. It best serves an organization to help the manager learn from their shortcomings so they can learn that this is what they should do for their direct reports, too.

虽然作为独立贡献者你能更控制分配给你的个人任务，但作为经理你负责让下属高效工作，同时让他们开心。在这样做时你会失败很多次。你的组织如何回应你的缺点将决定你如何回应你的下属。帮助经理从缺点中学习最有利于组织，这样他们也能学到这是他们应该对下属做的。

Keeping Things Professional保持专业

One of the most difficult things to do when you step into a manager's role for the first time is understanding when you should be a friend and when you should be a manager. This is an important trait to develop because at times there will be circumstances in which you must decide between being nice to a friend or being impartial in critiquing an employee's work. If not handled properly, it can potentially lead to the manager feeling a crisis in their ability to execute their job effectively, and you might end up losing some great employees and managers.

当你第一次踏入经理角色时最难做的事情之一是理解什么时候应该做朋友、什么时候应该做经理。这是一个需要发展的重要特质，因为有时你会遇到必须在对朋友好和公正批评员工工作之间做决定的情况。如果处理不当，可能导致经理感觉自己有效执行工作的能力出现危机，你可能最终失去一些优秀员工和经理。

Conflict Resolution冲突解决

When you put multiple people into any room, you now have multiple personalities, each with unique traits, thoughts, opinions, and ways of working. Depending on the pressures of the work, things will at some point begin to conflict. It is thus important for an organization to train the managers to deal with these situations. They need to be aware of when they need to step in and intervene, when and how to give feedback to the individuals involved in the conflict, when to take an unbiased stand, and when to escalate it, as well.

当你把多个人放进任何房间，你就有了多个个性，每个都有独特特质、想法、意见和工作方式。根据工作压力，事情在某个时候会开始冲突。因此组织培训经理处理这些情况很重要。他们需要意识到什么时候需要介入、什么时候以及如何给冲突中的个人反馈、什么时候采取不偏不倚的立场、以及什么时候升级。

Coming to Terms with Your Skills接受你的技能

One of the most difficult things to do in professional life is performing an honest self-assessment; not for the organization during appraisal time, but for yourself to assess whether what you're doing makes you happy. A good leader motivates people, looks for ways to unblock them, mentors them, and guides them through problems, and also recognizes when they are not the right person for the job. Accepting this as a reality will give you and your organization the opportunity to deal with it properly and set an example for future managers who go down the same path.

职业生涯中最难做的事情之一是做诚实的自我评估；不是在评估期间为组织做，而是为自己评估你在做的事情是否让你幸福。好的领导激励人、找方法为他们解除障碍、指导他们、引导他们解决问题，也认识到他们什么时候不是这份工作的合适人选。接受这一点作为现实会给你和组织机会妥善处理它，并为走同样道路的未来经理树立榜样。

— 第 159 页 —

Culture and management go hand in hand in any organization. How an organization defines its culture and cultivates its managers and seniors is what will define whether these individuals in turn will create an environment in which employees will be able to thrive and be creative, or an environment in which following the status quo and bullying/being bullied become the norm. In either case, it is important to remember the adage, "People leave bosses, not companies." Also true is, "People stick to bosses, not companies."

在任何组织中，文化和管理相辅相成。一个组织如何定义文化、培养经理和高级员工，将决定这些人反过来是创造一个员工能茁壮成长和有创造力的环境，还是一个维持现状和欺凌/被欺凌成为常态的环境。无论哪种情况，记住这句格言很重要：「人们离开老板，不是离开公司。」同样真实的是：「人们跟着老板，不是跟着公司。」
